commands.name: status
commands.description:
Report every provider's credential: where it comes from and whether it works. Never prints values.

Without --check only presence is reported (status `unchecked` or `missing`).
Exits 0 when every required provider is ok/unchecked (an optional one may be missing), 3 when any required provider has a problem or any credential is invalid/expired, 2 on a usage error.
A per-target provider (one credential per site/host/account) gets one entry per stored target, named `<kind>:<target>`.
The --json shape is a cross-tool contract: `tool`, `version`, `checked_at`, `credentials[]` with `provider`, `required`, `fields`, `source`, `source_ref`, `status`, `expires_at`, `quota`, `message`.

Example: semkit auth status --check --json

commands.name: lists
commands.description:
Word lists: without a command, every list with its source, lines and description.

A step takes a list as @NAME in an option that takes items.
A name is looked up in this order: the project's lists, then the folders of the variable SEMKIT_LISTS, then the folders of the config key lists, then the bundled lists.
SEMKIT_LISTS holds folders separated as in PATH; a relative one is from the current folder.
The config key lists holds a JSON list of folders; a relative one is from the project.

Example: semkit lists --json

commands.name: read
commands.description:
Read a table, run the steps in the order written, write the result: one pipeline.

Each step works on the current table. A change step rewrites the working column (with --as NAME it writes a new column NAME, which the next steps work on), a filter keeps or drops rows, a report (n-grams) makes its table the current one and its first text column the working one. After each step one line goes to stderr: the step, the rows before and after it, the cells it changed; the last line says how many rows went where. Every step and option is checked before the input is read.

Columns are read with the types of the file: numbers stay numbers, a text column is text and its empty cell an empty text. A column of numbers with spaces around a cell is numbers too. A column of numbers picked as the working column is text for the step and is written back as numbers. An option that takes items takes a comma list 'a,b', @FILE (one item per line, or the first column of a table without its header) or @NAME of a list (@stop/semtools, @minus/cheap…; `semkit lists` shows them all). `semkit read IN STEP --help` shows a step.

Example: semkit read core.csv remove-words --items купить dupes --kind lemmas --action drop write out.csv

options.name: --column
options.description: The working column the steps read and change; by default the first text column.

options.name: --whole
options.description: Read a text file as one cell of the column text (an article).

options.name: --trace
options.description: Write every cell a step changes and every row it drops to FILE as JSONL: row (1 is the first row under the header), step, column, before, after. An existing FILE needs --overwrite.

options.name: --dry-run

commands.name: ngrams
commands.description:
Every run of `n` words over all phrases, counted: a table ngram, count, docs, sum and forms.

The column count holds the occurrences; docs, in how many texts (rows of the input before split-text cut them) the gram occurs at least once; sum, with `weight`, the weight; forms, with `lemmas`, the word forms met for the gram, most frequent first, joined by ', ' («диваны, диван»), for a gram of several words its distinct spellings, at most 5.

The words are those of split-text: punctuation at the edges of a word is dropped («руб.» is «руб»), a sign such as ★ is no word, a number with inner points, commas or hyphens is one word («31.03.2026»). Sorted by count, biggest first, then by ngram. Words are compared in any case and with ё as е.
n: how many words in a gram.
lemmas: count lemmas of the words («диваны» is «диван»).
stopwords: on, every word counts; off (--no-stopwords), the grams are made of the words that are no stopwords, and a stopword between two of them stays inside the gram («купить диван в москве» gives «купить диван» and «диван в москве»); stopwords are found in any case.
weight: a column of numbers of the table (a frequency); sum adds its value once per occurrence.

The step counts the working column; the table replaces the current one, its column ngram is the working one.

Example: semkit read core.csv ngrams write out.csv

options.name: -n
options.description: how many words in a gram.

options.name: --lemmas
options.description: count lemmas of the words («диваны» is «диван»).

options.name: --stopwords

commands.name: bigrams
commands.description:
Pairs of words of a phrase in any order, counted: «купить диван» and «диван купить» both give «диван+купить».

Per phrase the words are sorted and a repeated word counts once. The table is that of ngrams.
lemmas: count lemmas of the words («диваны» is «диван»).
stopwords: on, every word counts; off (--no-stopwords), only the words that are no stopwords make pairs.
weight: a column of numbers of the table (a frequency); sum adds its value once per occurrence.

The step counts the working column; the table replaces the current one, its column ngram is the working one.

Example: semkit read core.csv bigrams write out.csv

commands.name: counts
commands.description:
One count per phrase, in a new column `<column>_<what>`.

what: "words" and "chars" — the words and the characters of the phrase; "count" — how many times the same phrase stands in the core; "number" — which occurrence of it this row is (1 for the first). Phrases are the same in any case and with ё as е; an empty cell has no count (an empty value). "share" — the cumulative share of the sum of `weight` (0..1) in row order; "share_of_total" — the value over the sum; both are rounded to 4 decimals and empty when the sum is 0. "abc" — the class by the cumulative share from the heaviest phrase down: "A" up to 80 %, "B" up to 95 %, "C" the rest. "share", "share_of_total" and "abc" need `weight`.
weight: the column of numbers to share (a frequency), for "share", "share_of_total" and "abc".

The step writes the count of each phrase to a new column <column>_count.

Example: semkit read core.csv counts words write out.csv

options.name: --what
options.description: "words" and "chars" — the words and the characters of the phrase; "count" — how many times the same phrase stands in the core; "number" — which occurrence of it this row is (1 for the first). "share" — the cumulative share of the sum of `weight` (0..1) in row order; "share_of_total" — the value over the sum; both are rounded to 4 decimals and empty when the sum is 0. "abc" — the class by the cumulative share from the heaviest phrase down: "A" up to 80 %, "B" up to 95 %, "C" the rest. "share", "share_of_total" and "abc" need `weight`.

options.name: --weight
options.description: the column of numbers to share (a frequency), for "share", "share_of_total" and "abc".

commands.name: insert
commands.description:
Text at the start and at the end of the phrase, as given; an empty phrase gets them too.

before: the text at the start («купить » gives «купить диван»).
after: the text at the end («диван» with « в москве» gives «диван в москве»).
each_word: round each word of the phrase instead («купить диван» with after "," → «купить, диван,»); the words are joined by one space and an empty phrase stays empty.

The step rewrites the working column; with --as NAME it writes the result to a new column NAME.

Example: semkit read core.csv insert --after ' в москве' write out.csv

The step rewrites the working column; with --as NAME it writes the result to a new column NAME.

Example: semkit read core.csv move-words @stop/wordstat write out.csv

commands.name: translit
commands.description:
Letters of one alphabet written in the other. The other chars stay.

to: "en" — «Щука жёлтая» → «Schuka zheltaya», a word in capitals stays in capitals («ЖУК» → «ZHUK»); "ru" — by letter groups, «Yandex» → «Яндекс», «Jeep» → «Джееп», «ob'em» → «обэм»: shch is щ, ts is ц, yy is ый («krasnyy» → «красный»), y after a vowel and before no vowel is й («Moy» → «Мой», «dayte» → «дайте»); a word in capitals is read by the groups of small letters and stays in capitals («ZHUK» → «ЖУК»). ь and ъ are dropped in "en" and е and ё both give e, so "ru" cannot bring them back («den» → «ден»).

The step rewrites the working column; with --as NAME it writes the result to a new column NAME.

Example: semkit read core.csv translit en write out.csv

commands.name: switch-layout
commands.description:

commands.name: compare-grams
commands.description:
How the grams of my text differ from the competitors' texts: a row per gram met in any competitor.

The density of a gram in a text is its count / the words of that text; a competitor without the gram counts as 0. Grams are those of ngrams. With lemmas, a word without a lemma (a single letter, an abbreviation or a unit: «г», «руб», «см») is in no gram, but counts in the words of a text.

lemmas: compare lemmas of the words («диваны» is «диван»).
stopwords: on, every word makes grams; off (the default), only the words that are no stopwords.
tolerance: how far from the norm a density is still within, a share of the norm (0.3 is ±30 %).
norm: «median» (the default) or «mean»: the density the verdict and the recommended occurrences go by.
words: the size of the text to recommend occurrences for, in words; by default the words of my text.
per_text: add a density column per competitor text, named by its url column when the table of the competitors has one, else text_1, text_2…
no_digits: leave out the words with a digit of every count, the words total included, as text-stats does.
exclude: words to leave out of every count the same way, as written, with case and ё folded, not by lemma.

The columns: ngram; docs, the competitors that hold it; docs_share, docs / competitors, 0..1; median, mean, min, max, the density in the competitors; mine, its density in my text; verdict, «below», «within» or «above», mine against norm x (1 ± tolerance), and when the norm is 0, «within» if mine is 0, else «above»; need, the norm x `words`, rounded to a whole number of occurrences; have, the occurrences in my text; add, need - have (negative: remove); med_count, the median number of occurrences in the competitors. Densities are rounded to 4 decimals. Sorted by median, biggest first, then ngram. With per_text, the density columns come last.

competitors: a file with the texts of the competitors, one per row, in its first text column; the file is read like `read` does. A url column, if the file has one, names the columns of --per-text.

commands.name: bm25
commands.description:
Okapi BM25 of each text for a query: one score per text, rounded to 4 decimals.

Terms are the lemmas without stopwords, on both sides; a term repeated in the query counts once. A word without a lemma (a single letter, an abbreviation or a unit: «г», «руб», «см») is no term. The length of a text is its number of terms. idf = ln((N - df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5) + 1); N, df and the average length are taken over the given texts, so to rank my text among the competitors give all of them together. score = sum over the terms of idf x tf x (k1 + 1) / (tf + k1 x (1 - b + b x length / average length)). A text without a term of the query scores 0.
query: the query, a phrase.
k1: how fast the score of a term saturates with its count (usually 1.2..2).
b: how much the length of a text lowers the score, 0..1 (0: not at all).

The step takes each cell of the working column as a text and writes its score for the query to a new column <column>_bm25; to rank my text among the competitors, put all the texts in the working column.

commands.name: coverage

Every distinct core phrase checked against the texts: a table phrase, count, docs, density and first.

mode: 'exact' — the words of the phrase in a row, case and ё folded; 'lemmas' — the same by lemmas of both sides; 'any_order' — the lemmas of the phrase all inside one piece of text (one phrase of split-text), in any order; a piece with them is one occurrence.

commands.name: decline
commands.description:
Every word of a phrase that declines, to the case: «купить красный диван» genitive → «купить красного дивана».

number: "singular" or "plural"; a phrase in the nominative plural declines in the plural anyway («угловые диваны» → «угловых диванов»).

An adjective and a noun in its lemma decline; a verb, an adverb, a preposition, a conjunction, a particle, an indeclinable word and a word already in another case («на дачу») stay; a pronoun declines only as an adjective («этот» → «этого», «он» stays). A feminine, neuter or plural adjective declines from its lemma («большая скидка» → «большой скидки»); a hyphenated noun declines whole («диван-кровать» → «дивана-кровати»). The accusative agrees by animacy: an inanimate noun and its adjective keep the nominative («купить кожаный диван»), an animate one takes the genitive («купить рыжего кота»). A word right after a preposition or a possessive pronoun that is not the first word stays («чехол для телефон» → «чехла для телефон»; «мой синий стол» → «моего синего стола»). A word in «-ой» before a word in another case stays too («с большой скидкой»). A word keeps its capitals.

commands.name: cluster-meaning
commands.description:
Clusters of phrases by meaning: phrases of close vectors share a cluster; every phrase gets one.

threshold: the similarity from 0 to 1 a phrase needs to the phrase that starts a cluster to join it.

The phrase with the most neighbours (phrases at the threshold or above) starts the first cluster and takes its neighbours; of the phrases left, the one with the most neighbours starts the next, and so on; a tie goes to the first row. A phrase without neighbours is a cluster of one. Equal phrases are one phrase. The clusters are numbered in the order of their first rows. The columns: cluster, cluster_name and similarity (of the phrase to the name of its cluster, 4 places); an empty cell gets none. The table tells the index it searched in `attrs["index"]`.

model: the encoder, pulled once with `semkit models pull NAME`: e5-small, bge-m3, potion, or hf:<id> of a model of the Hugging Face hub. Without --threshold the step takes the threshold of the model; a hub model has none.
freq: the column of the frequencies of the phrases in the current table; the cluster is named after its most frequent phrase. Without it, after the phrase nearest the centre of the cluster (the mean of its vectors).

The step adds the columns cluster, cluster_name and similarity right after the working column; the rows stay. Its summary names the index it searched: exact, or hnsw above about 300 000 phrases.

Example: semkit read core.csv cluster-meaning --freq freq write out.csv
